verdict.rationale: Vercel Workflows runs durable multi-step logic in the background. It retries failed steps, waits for external events, and resumes across crashes. Eve agents deployed on Vercel persist across interruptions and wait for tools or human input. Webhooks can trigger deployments on events. Together these give an event-driven way to run autonomous background automations, though each must be coded with an SDK or framework. Vercel Agent only takes approved actions, so it does not count as autonomous. Missing for 10: documented recurring schedules/cron for automations (the evidence only covers on-schedule page regeneration), a no-code or turnkey way to set up an automation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Vercel Workflows runs multi-step logic as durable code that can retry failed steps, wait for external events, and resume across crashes and deployments.
Build durable, observable applications and AI agents with the Workflow SDK on a fully managed platform.
Deploy an [eve](/eve) agent to Vercel to run conversations that persist across interruptions and wait for tools or human input.
Webhooks configured with Vercel can trigger a deployment when a specific event occurs.
